thread:
samir: Hey team — running into AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when a service assumes a cross-account role. Root call looks like: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --output text` and we get AccessDenied

alex: Are you using grants anywhere? If the service creates a grant and the decrypt call is using a grant token, you need to pass that token in the decrypt call.

samir: Not intentionally. The code path is an internal worker that calls AssumeRole -> uses temporary creds to call KMS. Logs show: `AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01`

jie: Two quick checks: (1) key policy allows the role ARN (not the assumed-session principal) or the root account. (2) any EncryptionContext expected by the key policy matches what you're sending. Context mismatch often yields AccessDenied.

samir: Key policy snippet I pasted below — can you scan?
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowAccountUse",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/infra-worker"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

adi: If the role is assumed cross-account, the effective principal is the role session (arn:aws:sts::222233334444:assumed-role/role-name/session-name). KMS key policies must reference the role ARN (not the assumed session) or the account principal. Your policy references the role in account 111122223333 — are you sure the role being assumed is in that same account?

samir: The flow is: service in account A (222233334444) assumes role in account B (111122223333) and then calls KMS in account B. The role ARN in B is `arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/infra-worker` — that matches the key policy.

alex: Ok. Next: do you use grants that are being created in the same call? Grants have two tricky things: (a) if the principal that created the grant later calls Decrypt, you either need to include the grant token returned by CreateGrant, or (b) the grant must be present in KMS at call time. If the client created the grant and immediately used Decrypt without the token, it can fail.

samir: We don't create grants in our code. It's just IAM role calling Decrypt.

jie: Check CloudTrail for KMS events — audit-bot should have logged a KMS:CreateGrant or KMS:Decrypt attempt with error reason.

audit-bot: link to CloudTrail event: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/home?region=us-west-2#/events/abcd1234 — shows Decrypt failed with AccessDenied, no CreateGrant prior.

adi: Another common cause: key policy denies requests that don't include a specific EncryptionContext value. Do your Decrypt calls include EncryptionContext? If the policy has a condition like `kms:EncryptionContext:...` an absent or different key will be denied.

samir: Our client doesn't set EncryptionContext. The app just hands KMS the ciphertext and zone id. Hm. I grepped the policy and found no encryptioncontext condition on the key.

alex: Then check IAM policy attached to the role. Even if key policy permits, an explicit deny in IAM (or a permission boundary) will block. Post the role's inline/policy doc?

samir: Role inline policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["sts:AssumeRole"], "Resource": "*" },
    { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01" }
  ]
}
```

jie: That looks ok. Did you confirm the role being assumed is the same name and that there isn't a permissions boundary attached to the role that strips kms:Decrypt?

samir: No boundary. Also confirmed role name.

adi: Another angle: is the KMS key multi-region or a custom key store? If it's a custom key store (in a CloudHSM), the Decrypt call might need extra permissions or the key material might be disabled. Also check key state (Enabled).

samir: Key state is ENABLED and CMK is in the expected region.

alex: Are you using the AWS SDK's default client after assume-role? If you keep the same client and only swap creds, some SDKs still sign with the original region/account. Try reinitializing the KMS client after assume-role.

samir: Good call — the worker reuses a singleton client. I'll rotate that to create a new KMS client with the temporary creds and retry.

(10m later)

samir: Update — re-created client, still AccessDenied. I captured the raw signed headers and compared — looks fine. CloudTrail shows the principal as `arn:aws:sts::222233334444:assumed-role/infra-worker/session123` calling Decrypt.

alex: Interesting — KMS will check the policy against the role, but when evaluating conditions like `aws:PrincipalOrgID` or `kms:CallerAccount`, the source account matters. Does the key policy restrict to `aws:PrincipalAccount` or similar?

samir: The policy had this extra statement I missed earlier:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowFromOpsAccount",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222233334444:root"},
  "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/role": "infra-worker"}}
}
```

jie: That Condition uses `aws:PrincipalTag/role` — tags on session principals are only present if the tag was passed at AssumeRole time and the session tags are allowed in the trust policy. If the assume-role call didn't pass that tag, the condition fails and KMS denies.

adi: Exactly. If the assumption doesn't pass that principal tag, KMS won't match the condition. Check the assume-role API call in CloudTrail: did it include `Tags` or `SessionTags`? Also trust policy must allow `sts:TagSession` or `sts:TagRole` etc.

samir: We were not passing session tags. I tried a quick test by calling AssumeRole with `--tags Key=role,Value=infra-worker` and re-called KMS with the resulting credentials — Decrypt succeeded.

alex: Nice find. So either remove that condition from the key policy or change the trust/assume flow to pass the tag. Also document behavior: session tags are not automatic.

samir: Will patch the worker to pass the session tag and also add a fallback clause to the key policy (allow the role ARN directly without tag) as a short-term fix.

security-bot: Filing a follow-up ticket sec-1628 to remove reliance on session tags for mission-critical decrypts.

samir: Thanks all — learned a lot about session tags + KMS conditions. Leaving this thread for the record.
